Now I'll write a reproducer: an admin request through `RequireAdmin` should get a non-nil `*store.User` from `UserFrom`.

{"title": "auth.RequireAdmin stores a User value in the context, so UserFrom returns nil and admin handlers panic", "body": "Reports: cr_a9759b (fp_b2a927), 2 crashes in v1.4.0 (commit 9c41e7a), DELETE /v1/admin/users/usr_ana, 2026-10-05 14:11-14:12.

Panic: nil pointer dereference at api/admin.go:15, in (*API).audit, on `admin.ID`.

Cause: auth/auth.go:39 in RequireAdmin does
    context.WithValue(r.Context(), userKey{}, *u)
which stores a store.User value. Require (line 23) stores the pointer u. UserFrom (line 45) asserts `ctx.Value(userKey{}).(*store.User)`. That assertion fails for the value, so UserFrom returns nil, and audit dereferences nil. Every admin route wrapped by RequireAdmin that calls audit (deleteUser, and any others) will panic for any authenticated admin.

Fix: at auth/auth.go:39, store `u` instead of `*u`. Add a test in auth that calls RequireAdmin with an admin token and checks UserFrom returns non-nil with ID "root".

Note: I could not apply the fix or add the test. Writes to auth/ are denied by the protected-path rule, so a person needs to make this change.", "fingerprint": "fp_b2a927", "root_cause": {"file": "auth/auth.go", "function": "RequireAdmin"}}
